slides.say: Given: x is bigger than y, and x times y is smaller than zero. Which of the following expressions is necessarily positive?

So x is bigger than y, and their product is negative. First, let's find which letter is positive and which is negative. Then [short pause] we'll solve it three ways, checking each fraction's signs, simplifying the fractions, and plugging in numbers.
[short pause] Let's start with the signs. x times y is negative, so one number is positive and the other negative. x is bigger than y, so x must be the positive one, and y must be the negative one.

Let's check choice number one. On top, x squared is positive. We subtract y, and y is negative, so subtracting it adds a positive amount. The whole top is positive. The bottom is y, which is negative. Positive over negative is negative, so this choice is out.
Now choice number two. On top, y minus x is negative minus positive, which is negative. The bottom is y, also negative. Negative over negative is positive. So choice number two is our answer.
at: choice number two is our answer

slides.say: [pause] Another way is to simplify each fraction first, then check the signs. From the givens, x and y have opposite signs. And x is bigger than y, so x is positive and y is negative.

Choice number one has x squared minus y, all over y. Divide each part on top by y. We get x squared over y, minus one. x squared over y is positive over negative, so it is negative. Subtracting one makes it even smaller. The result is negative, so this choice is out.
at: x squared over y, minus one

slides.say: Now choice number three. Use the difference-of-squares formula on top: x minus y, times x plus y. The bottom is x minus y, so that matching part cancels, leaving x plus y. x is positive and y is negative. Their sum can be positive, zero or negative, depending on their distances from zero. So it is not always positive. Out.
Choice number four has x times y on both the top and bottom. Cancel that matching part, leaving x over y. Positive over negative is negative, so this choice is out.

Now choice number two. Divide each part on top by y. y over y is one, so we get one minus x over y. x over y is negative. Subtracting a negative number adds a positive amount. So one minus x over y is always positive. Choice number two is our answer.

[pause] Now let's try plugging in. The product must be negative, so choose one positive number and one negative number. x must be the bigger one, so use x is one and y is negative one. Both givens work.
at: x is one and y is

slides.say: Choice number one has one minus negative one on top. That is one plus one, which is two. Two over negative one is negative two. It is not positive, so choice number one is out. Choice number two has negative one minus one on top, which is negative two. Negative two over negative one is two. It is positive, so this choice stays.

Choice number three has one minus one on top, so the whole fraction is zero. Zero is not positive, so choice number three is out. Choice number four gives negative one over one, which is negative one. It is not positive, so choice number four is out. Only choice number two remains. That is our answer, and we can stop without choosing another pair. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
